# John Edwards resignation is opportunity to appoint a regulator with teeth | Open Rights Group

[News](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/) John Edwards resignation is opportunity to appoint a regulator with teeth

## John Edwards resignation is opportunity to appoint a regulator with teeth

Open Rights Group has called for the Government to “appoint a regulator with teeth” following [John Edwards’ announcement](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7473590282803052544/) that he has resigned as Information Commissioner. His resignation comes after a workplace investigation into undisclosed allegations.

Open Rights Group’s Executive Director Jim Killock said:

“John Edward’s departure is a chance for the Government to appoint a regulator with teeth, and reset the regulators’ approach of providing data protection in name only.

“Parliament must ensure that the future Commission is run by professionals who want the law enforced, including against government data failures.”

“Edwards may now be offered jobs with Big Tech, the data industry and the very large legal firms who represent them, as many of his own senior staff and predecessors were. Edwards should set an example and refuse attractive salaries provided by this ‘revolving door’ – and the government should legislate to prevent this from happening so that the regulator is kept at arms length from Big Tech.”

## Re-set the ICO

Open Rights Group recently called for the [ICO to be re-set](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/campaign/reset-the-ico/) after multiple failings while Edwards was at the helm. These included introducing the [so-called public sector approach](https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/our-information/policies-and-procedures/public-sector-approach/) to enforcement, under which the ICO began to heavily rely on non-enforceable, written notices where the ICO point out that the law has been broken without taking any regulatory action to remedy an infringement or holding law-breakers to account.

As ORG’s alternative ICO annual report 2023-24 showed, [reprimands lacked](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/publications/ico-alternative-annual-report-2023-24/)[effectiveness and deterrence](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/publications/ico-alternative-annual-report-2023-24/). The ICO’s own [post-implementation review](https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/research-reports-impact-and-evaluation/impact-and-evaluation/evaluations/post-implementation-review-public-sector-approach-trial-september-2024/) of the public sector approach would later reveal how the volume of complaints raised by UK residents about public sector organisations’ use of their data has increased substantially as a result.

Edwards failed to open an investigation into the Ministry of Defence following a data leak that reportedly, led to [the death of at least 49 people](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/oct/27/afghan-data-leak-families-colleagues-killed) in the aftermath of the Taliban’s takeover of Afghanistan. This decision led to a [Parliamentary inquiry](https://committees.parliament.uk/work/9372/information-and-data-security-across-government-and-the-work-of-the-information-commissioner/publications/) from the DSIT Select Committee, and an open letter from 70+ data protection experts lamenting a [collapse in enforcement action](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/70-organisations-and-experts-demand-action-over-failing-ico/). Dame Chi Onwurah, the Chair of the Committee, acknowledged [the “institutional failure”](https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/50560/documents/275905/default/) that had led to the breach, which “raises serious questions for both the government and regulators like the ICO”.

Edwards was also supportive of the Government’s data protection reforms, which weakened the public’s rights and ability to **have co**ntrol over their personal data. The ICO was became the only regulator to fully support the government’s proposals despite concerns raised by the [Equality and Human Rights Commission](https://www.equalityhumanrights.com/media-centre/blogs/personal-data-rights-data-protection-and-digital-information-bill), the [National Data Guardian](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/619b84dde90e070445fd75ef/NDG_Data_A_New_Direction_Consultation_Response_v1.pdf), the [Biometrics Commissioner](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/data-a-new-direction-commissioners-response/dcms-consultation-data-a-new-direction-response-by-the-biometrics-and-surveillance-camera-commissioner-accessible-version), the [Scottish Biometrics Commissioner](https://www.biometricscommissioner.scot/news/commissioner-reiterates-concerns-about-data-protection-and-digital-information-no-2-bill-to-scottish-mp-on-westminster-committee/), and the [Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission](https://nihrc.org/publication/detail/nihrc-briefing-on-the-data-protection-and-digital-information-bill).

Read [The ICO isn’t doing its job – why the data watchdog needs to be reset](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/blog/the-ico-isnt-doing-its-job-why-the-data-watchdog-needs-to-be-reset/).

translated_article_markdown_zh:
# John Edwards 辭職後，英國有機會任命更有力的監管者

## John Edwards 辭職後，英國有機會任命更有力的監管者

在 [John Edwards 宣布](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7473590282803052544/)辭去資訊專員（Information Commissioner）一職後，Open Rights Group 呼籲英國政府「任命一位有實權的監管者」。他的辭職發生在一項針對未公開指控的職場調查之後。

Open Rights Group 執行長 Jim Killock 表示：

「John Edwards 離任，是英國政府任命一位有實權的監管者、重新設定監管機關做法的機會。過去的做法只是名義上提供資料保護。」

「國會必須確保未來的委員會由真正希望法律被執行的專業人士來運作，包括針對政府的資料失誤執法。」

「Edwards 接下來可能會像許多他的高階幕僚與前任一樣，獲得科技巨頭、資料產業，以及代表這些企業的大型法律事務所延攬。Edwards 應該樹立榜樣，拒絕這種『旋轉門』提供的優渥薪資；英國政府也應立法防止這種情況發生，讓監管機關與科技巨頭保持適當距離。」

## 重新設定 ICO

Open Rights Group 最近呼籲[重新設定 ICO](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/campaign/reset-the-ico/)，原因是在 Edwards 掌舵期間，ICO 出現多項失職。其中包括在執法上導入[所謂的公共部門做法](https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/our-information/policies-and-procedures/public-sector-approach/)；在這套做法下，ICO 開始高度依賴不具強制力的書面通知，只指出法律遭到違反，卻沒有採取任何監管行動來補救侵害，也沒有追究違法者責任。

正如 ORG 的 2023-24 年替代版 ICO 年度報告所示，這些[申誡缺乏](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/publications/ico-alternative-annual-report-2023-24/)[效果與嚇阻力](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/publications/ico-alternative-annual-report-2023-24/)。ICO 自己後來對公共部門做法所做的[實施後檢討](https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/research-reports-impact-and-evaluation/impact-and-evaluation/evaluations/post-implementation-review-public-sector-approach-trial-september-2024/)也顯示，英國居民針對公共部門組織使用其資料所提出的申訴量，因此大幅增加。

在一場據報導導致塔利班接管阿富汗後[至少 49 人死亡](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/oct/27/afghan-data-leak-families-colleagues-killed)的資料外洩事件後，Edwards 未對國防部展開調查。這項決定引發 DSIT 特別委員會的[國會調查](https://committees.parliament.uk/work/9372/information-and-data-security-across-government-and-the-work-of-the-information-commissioner/publications/)，也促成 70 多位資料保護專家發出公開信，感嘆[執法行動崩解](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/70-organisations-and-experts-demand-action-over-failing-ico/)。該委員會主席 Dame Chi Onwurah 承認，導致這起外洩事件的是一場[「制度性失靈」](https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/50560/documents/275905/default/)，這也「對政府以及 ICO 這類監管機關提出嚴肅問題」。

Edwards 也支持英國政府的資料保護改革，而這些改革削弱了公眾的權利，以及**掌控**自己個人資料的能力。儘管[平等與人權委員會](https://www.equalityhumanrights.com/media-centre/blogs/personal-data-rights-data-protection-and-digital-information-bill)、[國家資料守護者](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/619b84dde90e070445fd75ef/NDG_Data_A_New_Direction_Consultation_Response_v1.pdf)、[生物辨識委員](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/data-a-new-direction-commissioners-response/dcms-consultation-data-a-new-direction-response-by-the-biometrics-and-surveillance-camera-commissioner-accessible-version)、[蘇格蘭生物辨識委員](https://www.biometricscommissioner.scot/news/commissioner-reiterates-concerns-about-data-protection-and-digital-information-no-2-bill-to-scottish-mp-on-westminster-committee/)，以及[北愛爾蘭人權委員會](https://nihrc.org/publication/detail/nihrc-briefing-on-the-data-protection-and-digital-information-bill)都提出疑慮，ICO 仍成為唯一完全支持政府提案的監管機關。
